strengths: Excellent reuse: upload_resident, dispatch_resident, and readback_resident are designed as thin wrappers over allocate_device_local_buffer, allocate_staging_buffer_cached, round_up_pow2, and allocate_descriptor_pool_and_set — all of which already have extensive unit-test coverage (AT-803, AT-804, AT-1407h/i/j, AT-1420). No logic is duplicated.

ResidentBuffers struct in resident.rs is a clean, already-present skeleton that captures every Vulkan object the three methods will need (device_local_bufs, staging_bufs, descriptor_set/pool, command_buffer, command_pool, fence, query_pool, timestamp_period, timestamp_valid_bits, queue_family_index, uses_coopmat). Drop impl is already implemented and correct, using fence-wait before destroying any object.

Timing methodology (HN-6) is explicitly addressed: cmd_reset_query_pool is the FIRST recorded command in the dispatch_resident CB in the same submission, before either write_timestamp. This matches Vulkan spec §18.2 (Query Operations — vkCmdResetQueryPool must be called in the same command buffer and must be before the corresponding vkCmdWriteTimestamp), which ARM (Mali GPU Best Practices) and NVIDIA Vulkan libraries both require.

masked_timestamp_delta is already implemented and tested (AT-1535) — hardware counter wrap-around is handled correctly for all valid_bits values including 0 and 64. This removes a frequent source of incorrect GPU timing on NVIDIA hardware (32-bit timer wrap at ~4 seconds).

CB/fence/query-pool reuse across N is architecturally enforced: the design allocates exactly one CB from a RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER pool at upload time and calls reset_command_buffer + reset_fences + cmd_reset_query_pool inside dispatch_resident before each re-record. This is the same pattern used by Vulkan-Samples (https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Samples/blob/main/samples/performance/timestamp_queries/) and avoids the per-iteration alloc growth AT-1571 measures.

Descriptor set ownership is cleanly separated: ResidentBuffers creates its own pool+set via the same allocate_descriptor_pool_and_set function used by KernelHandleInner, bound to its own device-local buffers — completely independent of handle.inner.descriptor_set. This allows a single KernelHandle (pipeline+layout) to serve both dispatch_handle and multiple concurrent ResidentBuffers without aliasing, matching the Vulkan spec guidance that descriptor sets are 'allocated from descriptor pools' and can coexist freely (Vulkan spec §14.2.3).

prepare_kernel_checked is correctly additive: it delegates to the existing prepare_kernel after running typed preflight. The factored preflight_kernel_support private helper avoids duplicating the coopmat/feature logic. This follows the open/closed principle and avoids any signature change on the existing public API.

panic->typed-error conversion (D) is the right approach: scalar_ty_to_coopmat_scalar_meta returning DriverError::UnsupportedCoopmatScalar with a String-typed ScalarTy representation avoids leaking the HIR enum into the public error surface, consistent with how the rest of axc-driver wraps internal types.

Strategy-hole resolution via compile_source_with_assignments with pinned {tile_m:1, tile_n:1} is correct: tile_m=1 / tile_n=1 IS the first/default candidate value in the @strategy ?[1,2,4] set, so the generated SPIR-V is semantically equivalent to 'run matmul with one output element per invocation' — a valid (if untuned) matmul. No autotuner is required; the bench explicitly documents this as the baseline and defers tiling to M3.4.

50 GB cap is respected: 3 x 4096^2 x 4 bytes (f32) = 192 MB device-local + at most 192 MB staging for the output = ~384 MB total. The design adds a bench-time assertion and a dynamic size-shrink guard for the wg_x > max_compute_work_group_count[0] edge case (with 4096^2/64 = 262144 exceeding the Vulkan mandatory minimum of 65535 in x). The shrink-to-largest-pow2 strategy is correct.

queue_submit_lock (CRITICAL-5) is preserved: every queue_submit in the three resident methods must be under self.queue_submit_lock per handoff note HANDOFF-5, which is explicitly called out and matches the invariant enforced throughout dispatch_single_queue and dispatch_dedicated.

Anti-pattern #9 (no mocking GPU execution) is respected: all resident-path tests (AT-1530/1531/1570/1571/1572) are #[ignore]-gated and require AXC_ENABLE_GPU_TESTS=1. CI uses Lavapipe (software GPU) as the real-GPU fallback, which satisfies the spirit of the rule.

AT-1573 (timing source selection) is a pure unit test runnable without GPU. The factored select_timing_source(valid_bits, period) helper makes this testable and the test runs in the normal (non-ignored) cargo test pass, providing fast feedback.

HANDOFF-6 (get_query_pool_results with WAIT flag) is belt-and-suspenders: WAIT on get_query_pool_results avoids any potential NOT_READY race even though the fence wait already guarantees completion. This matches what NVIDIA's Vulkan timestamp query samples do (https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Samples/blob/main/samples/performance/timestamp_queries/timestamp_queries.cpp).
concerns: Minor: The existing bench file (resident_matmul.rs) calls compile_source_with_meta for MATMUL_F32_SRC (line 155), which will fail at the UnresolvedStrategyHole backstop. The design correctly identifies this and the fix (switch to compile_source_with_assignments) is clear. Coder must ensure the bench COMPILES with the strategy hole fix before the GPU dispatch logic is added; otherwise the bench build fails entirely and AT-1577 regression-gate fires.

Minor: readback_resident reuses resident.command_buffer to record the readback copy+barrier, then submits it on a fresh fence-wait cycle. This is correct but means the CB that dispatch_resident just used for the compute pass is reset again for the readback. The design addresses this (HANDOFF-4: reset before re-recording) but the Coder must ensure that if dispatch_resident was called last and the fence is signaled, reset_command_buffer is called before readback records into the same CB. The existing Drop impl already does a wait_for_fences before destruction, so there is no lifetime hazard — but the coder should add a // SAFETY comment noting the CB is not in-flight at the start of readback_resident.

Minor: The upload_resident spec says 'transient upload staging+CB' for the one-time input copy, but the resident.rs skeleton already allocates per-slot StagingBuffer via the staging_bufs Vec. The design should clarify whether the upload uses the pre-allocated staging_bufs[i] (populated at upload time) or a truly transient staging buffer. Given that staging_bufs is described as being for readback only (output slots), the upload should use a separate transient staging buffer or optionally reuse the readback staging if the slot is both read and written. HANDOFF-1 says 'no duplication beyond minimal cmd_copy_buffer calls' and the spec says 'transient staging buffer, free after upload' — the coder should confirm the input-upload staging is separate from the readback-staging (already in staging_bufs) to avoid aliasing the readback mapping with the upload copy.

Minor: The bench currently calls ctx.prepare_kernel (unchecked) for MATMUL_F32_SRC even after the migration to the resident API. The design says the bench should switch dispatch_resident_matmul_tile to use prepare_kernel_checked with coopmat preflight. The matmul_tflops_4096 bench does not need coopmat (f32 tiled), so calling prepare_kernel_checked with coopmat=None is equivalent to prepare_kernel — this is fine. The coder should be explicit about which kernel goes through which prepare path.

Minor: The spec says the readback_resident CB is reset from the same CB that dispatch_resident used. If the caller has not called dispatch_resident before readback_resident (e.g., doing upload+readback without any dispatch), the fence may be in an unsignaled state from upload (the upload sets the fence to signaled after the upload CB). The design should clarify the expected call order contract (upload → dispatch(s) → readback). Adding a check or a documented precondition is sufficient.

Very minor: HANDOFF-12 mentions asserting bench buffer total < 50 GB before allocation. The spec already shows 192 MB for 4096^2 f32 x3 is well under the cap, but the assert is good practice. The coder should place it before the allocate_device_local_buffer calls in upload_resident when called from the bench (or as a bench-level guard), not inside the library method itself (library should not encode the 50 GB cap as a hard assert — that is a project policy, not a Vulkan constraint).
validation_against_existing: allocate_descriptor_pool_and_set (kernel_handle.rs line 293-328) is already pub(crate) and takes exactly (device, dsl, buffer_count) — the upload_resident descriptor allocation can call it directly for ResidentBuffers without any new code. The pool_size / alloc_info pattern mirrors the existing prepare_kernel call at context.rs line 787-793.

The descriptor write loop in ensure_buffers_fit_with_mem_props (kernel_handle.rs lines 439-453) is the canonical reference for the resident descriptor writes: dst_set, dst_binding = binding_plan.buffers[i].buffer_position, STORAGE_BUFFER, WHOLE_SIZE. upload_resident must use the same binding_idx = handle.inner.binding_plan.buffers[i].buffer_position.

The RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER pattern for resident CBs is already used on the context's command_pool (context.rs line 591-592): CommandPoolCreateFlags::RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER. The resident pool is a second pool on the same queue family with the same flag — this is a Vulkan-standard approach and does not require any new capability.

queue_submit_lock serialization is already in place for all queue submits in dispatch_single_queue (kernel_handle.rs line 840) and dispatch_dedicated (kernel_handle.rs lines around 1143+). The resident methods must acquire the same lock before each vkQueueSubmit.

timestamp_period and compute_timestamp_valid_bits are already stored on VulkanContext (context.rs lines 239-245) and exposed via pub accessors (lines 716-725). upload_resident can snapshot them into ResidentBuffers without any new infrastructure.
binding_is_readback is already defined (used in single-queue and dedicated dispatch paths in kernel_handle.rs). readback_resident uses the same predicate for its Lever A check — consistent with HN-9.

The existing bench bench_matmul_tflops_4096 already has sample_size(3) and iter_custom (lines 195-233), and the effective_tflops helper is already present (lines 44-47). The only code change needed is replacing compile_source_with_meta with compile_source_with_assignments and switching from dispatch_handle to the resident API.
external_references: Vulkan spec §18.2 (Query Operations): vkCmdResetQueryPool must appear in the same command buffer before vkCmdWriteTimestamp — https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html#queries-operation-time

Vulkan spec §14.2.3 (Descriptor Sets): multiple descriptor sets can be allocated from the same pool or from independent pools; they do not alias — https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html#descriptorsets-sets
Vulkan spec §3.3.3 (Object Lifetime): VkDevice must be destroyed before its parent VkInstance — already enforced in context.rs via ManuallyDrop

KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Samples timestamp_queries sample (uses same cmd_reset_query_pool-first pattern in the recorded CB): https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Samples/blob/main/samples/performance/timestamp_queries/timestamp_queries.cpp
ARM Mali Vulkan Best Practices (timestamp wrap handling, reset ordering): https://developer.arm.com/documentation/101897/latest/
NVIDIA Nsight documentation on GPU timestamp queries and timestampPeriod: https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-systems/
rspirv crate (used for SPIR-V emission in this project): https://github.com/gfx-rs/rspirv — no new SPIR-V capabilities are required for M3.1.5 (pure runtime milestone)

Vulkan spec §10.3 (Queue family ownership transfer): QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED in buffer barriers is correct when both queues are the same family (single-queue mode) — https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html#synchronization-queue-transfers

open_question_positions.OQ1_warmup: AGREE with Architect's recommendation: 2 warm-up dispatch_resident calls before the measured loop in both the bench and AT-1530. For the bench (iter_custom path), >=1 untimed warm-up is essential because the first dispatch_resident pays pipeline warm-up, first-touch page-in on device-local memory (NVIDIA GDDR7 page fault on first write from a freshly-bound buffer), and GPU frequency ramp. Recommend min-of-N (N=10 for bench, N>=3 for AT-1530) rather than avg, because outliers skew avg on a GPU that throttles briefly. Criterion's iter_custom loop already handles multiple samples; the coder just needs to prepend >=2 untimed calls and then start the timing loop.
open_question_positions.OQ2_independent_descriptor_set: STRONGLY AGREE: the ResidentBuffers owning its own descriptor pool+set (independent of handle.inner.descriptor_set) is the only clean design. Reusing handle.inner.descriptor_set would couple the resident and dispatch_handle buffer pools, requiring either mutual exclusion or a refcount — both are worse than the current approach. A single KernelHandle backing multiple independent ResidentBuffers (one per benchmark run, or one per thread in a future M3.3 parallel runner) is the correct model. This is validated by how descriptor pools work in Vulkan: each pool is independent, and allocating from two pools into the same DSL is explicitly supported by the spec.
open_question_positions.OQ3_uses_coopmat_default: AGREE: false default is acceptable and correct. uses_coopmat is #[allow(dead_code)] diagnostic-only and the field has no semantic effect on dispatch. The KernelHandle does not currently carry a 'was this built from coopmat source' flag, and adding one would require a new field on KernelHandleInner — which is out of M3.1.5 scope. false is the safe default (it is a 'shaderInt16 diagnostic' according to the resident.rs comment, which is mislabeled; the field name is uses_coopmat but the comment says shaderInt16, so the Coder should also fix the field doc comment to reflect its actual diagnostic purpose).
open_question_positions.OQ4_prepare_time_vs_dispatch_time: AGREE with prepare-time gating via prepare_kernel_checked. The preflight catches incompatibilities before any SPIR-V is submitted, giving a clear typed error to the caller and avoiding a wasted GPU submit. prepare_kernel_checked is additive and does not change dispatch_handle. Dispatch-time gating would require threading coopmat metadata through the dispatch arguments (breaking the dispatch_handle signature) or storing it on the handle (adding a field). Prepare-time is strictly cleaner. The only caveat is that prepare_kernel_checked requires the caller to have the CoopMatShapeMeta at prepare time, which they do (it comes from compile_source_with_meta).

test_suggestions: Consider adding AT-1578 (a unit test for preflight_kernel_support isolation): construct a synthetic EnabledDeviceFeatures with specific fields false and verify that preflight_kernel_support returns the correct DeviceFeatureUnsupported variant. This test is pure (no GPU) and covers the HANDOFF-7 requirement that the first missing feature reported is deterministic (declaration order of EnabledDeviceFeatures bools).

AT-1571 (CB/fence/query-pool handle invariance across N dispatches) is excellent; also verify that device-local buffer VkBuffer handles in resident.device_local_bufs are unchanged after N dispatches (i.e., no accidental reallocation in the dispatch path). This is a cheap pointer comparison.

For AT-1570 (round-trip correctness vs dispatch_handle): ensure the test uses a kernel with at least one ReadOnly binding so that Lever A is exercised in the comparison path — otherwise the test does not cover the case where readback_resident emits an empty Vec for that slot while dispatch_handle emits non-empty output_sizes.
summary: M3.1.5 is a well-scoped, architecturally clean milestone that correctly completes the GPU-resident benchmark infrastructure. All four sub-tasks (A–D) reuse existing machinery rather than duplicating it, the timing methodology is sound (HN-6, timestamp wrap, GPU/CPU fallback), the API is additive-only, and the test coverage is thorough across both unit-level (AT-1573, AT-1575) and GPU-integration (AT-1530/1531/1570/1571/1572) levels. The strategy-hole fix is the minimal correct solution (pin default candidate, document, defer real tiling to M3.4). Concerns are all minor and process-level (upload staging clarification, call-order contract for readback, bench compile ordering). The design is ready to proceed to the Pessimistic Design Reviewer and then to Coder.
